subject: Mutual action plan: staggered pool sizing, lead-time hedges & close milestones
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@stellarsystems.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stellarsystems.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask — lead times & MAP for private GPU pool

Mina — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and asks from our side as we move toward a 4Q close: 

1) Lead times: Stellar needs explicit lead-time windows for Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). We have constrained procurement windows and need to align delivery tranches. Please confirm typical procurement-to-ready timings and any hedges you recommend.

2) Sizing: we plan to start with a smaller private pool and scale. Can you propose a staggered pool-sizing plan (initial staging, canary, full commit) with quantifiable throughput targets (tokens/sec) and fallback options?

3) Docs: procurement will need a MAP with milestones, a SOC2 evidence checklist, and a PO path / sample SOW. Can you share a working draft we can circulate to procurement?

Target: internal execs want a commitment decision by 2026-12-10. If Redwood can provide a MAP and clear lead-time hedges this week, procurement can prioritize.

Appreciate a short MAP draft and a capacity model we can review.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of ML Infrastructure
Stellar Systems

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@stellarsystems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask — lead times & MAP for private GPU pool

Alex — thanks, this is clear and achievable. Attached is a working mutual action plan (MAP_draft_v1.pdf) and a capacity model (capacity_model_v2.csv) keyed to the three-stage plan we discussed. High-level summary below: 

TL;DR: Recommended path = staggered commit with 3 tranches (canary, ramp, steady-state). We hedge lead-time risk by reserving a small Dedicated slice for production-critical traffic until the private pool is fully provisioned.

Milestones (proposed):
- Week 0 (Dec 1): MAP signed and PO triggered (Procurement starts).
- Week 2 (Dec 15): SOC2 questionnaire logged; initial MSA redlines exchanged.
- Week 6 (Jan 12): Canary tranche live (8x A800/H100-equivalent vCPUs; see model for perf targets).
- Week 10 (Feb 9): Ramp tranche live (additional 16 cards) — target 60% of steady-state throughput.
- Week 16 (Mar 29): Steady-state (full pool) — 32 cards (example sizing), autoscale configured.

Lead-time notes (typical):
- Dedicated slice (reserved hosted capacity): 1–2 weeks to reserve and validate for production routing. Acts as an escape hatch.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): 10–16 weeks depending on region (networking + KMS + acceptance tests). If we concurrent-order networking and procurement we can push to the lower end.

Fallbacks and hedges:
- Keep an SLO-backed Dedicated reserve for 90 days post GO-LIVE, then transition traffic by % cutover.
- Quantized model variants (int8) for early traffic to reduce GPU footprint if onboarding slips.

Attachments: MAP_draft_v1.pdf, capacity_model_v2.csv, SOC2_questions.xlsx (the SOC2 file is the questionnaire Stellar procurement asked for; filled sections are marked). 

Next steps: I can convert this MAP into a one-page milestone checklist for procurement and a compact SOW template for legal if that helps the timeline.

If you want, I can loop in Marissa on acceptance criteria and Lauren on on-prem network telemetry for the acceptance gate.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_draft_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: capacity_model_v2.csv (csv)]
[Attachment: SOC2_questions.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Stellar MAP & capacity ask — recommended approach

Team — looping you in for quick alignment; Alex from Stellar wants a MAP + explicit lead-time hedges; target commitment decision 2026-12-10. Key asks below; please reply with any objections by EOD tomorrow.

Customer asks and our recommended responses:
- They need deterministic lead-times for Private (VPC/on-prem). We should commit to the "10–16 weeks" window but provide an acceleration plan (parallel networking procurement + prebooking hardware via Dedicated).
- Staggered sizing: we recommend 3 tranches: Canary (8 cards), Ramp (+16), Steady (+8–+? to reach target). See capacity_model_v2.csv for perf numbers.
- Acceptance gating: define three acceptance checks — smoke perf, KV cache stability under 10k concurrent sessions, and end-to-end latency for p95 < 350ms. Marissa, can you scope test harness for the KV/latency checks and estimate time?
- Commercial: suggest a 12-month commitment with an optional staged billing (billing starts on production cutover per tranche). Ben — please draft the price table and an optional Dedicated-bridge credit (first 90 days) to reduce risk.

I'll send the customer the one-page milestone checklist we discussed and the SOW template after Ben and Marissa confirm numbers.

Thanks,
Mina

From: Alex Chen <alex@stellarsystems.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stellarsystems.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Re: Initial ask — lead times & MAP for private GPU pool

Mina — this looks good and addresses our main concerns. A couple of follow-ups before we circulate to procurement: 

- Can you convert the milestones into calendar dates (we need firm checkpoints for procurement to lock budgets)? Suggest the dates align to the ones you listed (I'll map to our internal calendar).
- Procurement will want a sample SOW and an estimate of total TCO in the first 12 months (including Dedicated-bridge credits if included).
- SOC2: thanks for the questionnaire. Please highlight which evidence items we must supply vs Redwood provides.

If you can send a one-page MAP with dates and a short SOW sketch by tomorrow morning, procurement will prioritize the review and aim to return a PO by 2026-12-08.

Appreciate the rapid turn — happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

—Alex
